our_result: C->M cadence +4.58% n.s.; C->T+M cadence +4.25% p=0.0312
corrected_interpretation: Metronome cue increased cadence directionally; combined condition showed significant cadence increase.

corrected_interpretation: IMU shock proxy did not decrease despite step-rate increase; interpret as contrast to typical loading-reduction literature.
supported_fact: Increasing step rate shortened step length and reduced braking impulse, peak vertical GRF at +10%, and impact transient occurrence.

corrected_interpretation: PF peak increase indicates ankle posture/foot placement/strike strategy change; not direct push-off power evidence.
supported_fact: Forefoot strike runners land with a more plantarflexed ankle and show greater gastrocnemius activity in terminal swing.
does_not_support: Does not show metronome causes PF increase or push-off power increase.

our_result: PF peak increased under metronome/combined conditions
corrected_interpretation: Plantarflexors are relevant to running propulsion, but PF angle alone cannot prove propulsive force/power.
supported_fact: Running simulations identify plantarflexor muscles as important contributors to support/propulsion.
does_not_support: Does not validate PF angle peak as push-off force in this experiment.

our_result: Report uses Thaut for gastrocnemius EMG timing
corrected_interpretation: Use Thaut only for auditory cueing effects on temporal gait and gastrocnemius EMG in stroke walking; not running push-off proof.
supported_fact: Rhythmic auditory cueing affected temporal stride parameters and gastrocnemius EMG patterns in hemiparetic gait.
does_not_support: Does not support running plantarflexion or push-off increase in healthy runners.

corrected_interpretation: External cueing altered temporal control; present data show variability increased, especially T->T+M.

does_not_support: Does not prove same effect in this exact running/taping protocol.

corrected_interpretation: Do not claim pelvis stabilization; RAS evidence is mainly spatiotemporal gait outcomes.
supporting_paper: Thaut et al. 2007; Yu et al. 2015

does_not_support: Does not directly support pelvis pitch/roll SD improvement.

supporting_paper: Cordova et al. 2000; Chinn et al. 2014

supporting_paper: Heiderscheit et al. 2011 plus present data

does_not_support: Does not support strong causal offset mechanism.
